newsitem.title: USA: Kiwi Int'l says gets new backer for financing plan.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi Int'l says gets new backer for financing plan.

text.p: Kiwi International Airlines said on Friday that ISBRE Holding Co has agreed to put up $5 million to put the bankrupt carrier back in the air.
US Bankruptcy Judge Rosemary Gambardella agreed to hear the proposal from ISBRE and set a November 22 hearing for the ISBRE plan.

"I am very optimistic that we will be able to get the airline back into business within weeks. ISBRE is a very substantial company, as opposed to companies which have previously shown interest in investment," said Kiwi president and chief executive Jerry Murphy.
Murphy said ISBRE is a private company that "knows about aviation."
It owns merican Helicopters, based in Linden New Jersey, and also imports bottled water from Norway. It is also involved in entertainment and financial companies, he said.

If the plan is accepted next Friday, seven of the airline's 15 aircraft should be back in the air and perhaps 600 of the 1,200 laid off employees should be back working, Murphy said. The Newark-based carrier sought Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on September 30 and suspended scheduled operations on October 15.
